items.stem: A ray of light travels from air into glass. The refractive index of glass is $1.50$ and the angle of incidence is $40.0^\circ$. What is the angle of refraction?
items.hint: Using Snell's law, $1 \times \sin 40.0^\circ = 1.50 \times \sin r$, so $\sin r = \sin 40.0^\circ / 1.50 = 0.4285$ and $r = 25.4^\circ$. Dividing the angle by $1.50$ gives $26.7^\circ$. Leaving the angle unchanged gives $40.0^\circ$. Swapping the indices gives $\sin r = 1.50 \times \sin 40.0^\circ$, so $r = 74.6^\circ$.

items.stem: The speed of light in a liquid is $2.21 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The speed of light in vacuum is $3.00 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. What is the refractive index of the liquid?
items.hint: $n = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3.00 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}}{2.21 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}} = 1.36$, to 3 significant figures. Option A is $\dfrac{v}{c}$.

items.stem: A coin lies at the bottom of a tank of liquid. Its real depth is $12.0\ \text{cm}$. Viewed from directly above in air, its apparent depth is $8.00\ \text{cm}$. What is the refractive index of the liquid?
items.hint: $n = \dfrac{\text{real depth}}{\text{apparent depth}} = \dfrac{12.0\ \text{cm}}{8.00\ \text{cm}} = 1.50$. Option A is the reciprocal. Option C is the difference of the depths in centimetres. Option D is their sum.
